uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0533.explanation: Zinc is more easily oxidized, so it is the anode (left side). Copper is the cathode (right side). The notation is: anode | oxidized species || reduced species | cathode.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0534.explanation: Molecules that have permanent dipoles are attracted to each other. The positive end of one is attracted to the negative end of the other, and vice versa. These forces are only important when molecules are close to each other.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0535.explanation: Rutherford discovered the nuclear nature of the atom, leading to the acceptance of the picture of the atom as a 'microscopic solar system' in which electrons orbited the nucleus.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0536.explanation: Thermochemistry is a branch of thermodynamics that focuses on energy changes (especially heat) that accompany chemical reactions and physical processes.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0537.explanation: When n = 3, there are three permissible values of l: 0, 1, and 2, corresponding to s, p, and d subshells.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0538.explanation: The dissociation of dinitrogen tetroxide into nitrogen dioxide is endothermic (ΔH > 0). The answer key states +14 kcal.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0539.explanation: In precise work, the specific heat of water is often taken as 4.184 J/g·°C.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0540.explanation: The trigonal planar geometry of SP2 hybrid orbitals results in bond angles of 120°.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0541.explanation: London dispersion forces are present in all molecules due to temporary dipoles. Their strength increases with molecular size and polarizability.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0542.explanation: Dipole-dipole interactions occur between polar molecules. Polar molecules have a permanent separation of charge, creating a partial positive end (δ+) and a partial negative end (δ-). These opposite partial charges attract each other.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0543.explanation: Elements in the same group (vertical column) have similar chemical properties due to having the same number of valence electrons.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0544.explanation: Molar heat capacity (C_m) is the heat required to raise 1 mole of a substance by 1°C.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0545.explanation: Giant covalent structures have high melting and boiling points because strong covalent bonds require a large amount of energy to break.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0546.explanation: A very small equilibrium constant (K << 1) means that the ratio of products to reactants is very small. This indicates that at equilibrium, the mixture contains mostly reactants, so the reactants dominate.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0548.explanation: Fe + CuSO4(aq) → FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s) is a displacement reaction where iron displaces copper from copper sulfate.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0549.explanation: Density = mass/volume = 50.208 g / 5.6 mL = 8.9657 g/mL. Volume has 2 significant figures, so the answer should have 2 significant figures: 9.0 g/mL.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0550.explanation: Molar mass C₃H₈ = 44.1 g/mol. Moles C₃H₈ = 96.1 g / 44.1 g/mol = 2.18 mol. From equation, 1 mol C₃H₈ reacts with 5 mol O₂, so moles O₂ = 2.18 mol × 5 = 10.9 mol. Mass O₂ = 10.9 mol × 32.0 g/mol = 348.8 g ≈ 349 g.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0551.explanation: Gases are one of the three common states of matter, along with solids and liquids.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0553.explanation: Factors affecting gas pressure include temperature, volume of the container, and number of gas particles.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0554.explanation: The atom that loses electrons becomes a positively charged cation; the atom that gains electrons becomes a negatively charged anion.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0555.explanation: Boiling is rapid vaporization that occurs throughout the bulk liquid at a fixed temperature (the boiling point). Evaporation occurs at the surface of a liquid at temperatures below the boiling point, involving only particles with sufficient kinetic energy to escape.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0556.explanation: A sigma (σ) bond is formed by end-to-end overlap of orbitals, resulting in electron density concentrated along the internuclear axis, which is generally stronger and has more effective overlap than the lateral overlap of a pi (π) bond.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0557.explanation: Stoichiometry is the branch of chemistry that deals with the quantitative relationships between reactants and products in a chemical reaction, based on the balanced chemical equation.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0558.explanation: Most molecular compounds are insoluble in water because they release too little energy when they dissolve to overcome the intermolecular forces. They are often soluble in organic solvents because both the molecular compound and the organic solvent experience van der Waals forces, allowing for favorable interactions.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0559.explanation: Endothermic reactions absorb heat from the surroundings. The products have higher enthalpy (potential energy) than the reactants, so ΔH = H_products - H_reactants is positive.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0560.explanation: The hybridization of atomic orbitals takes place either by reshuffling of all or some of the orbitals in the excited state.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0561.explanation: Gases exert pressure on all surfaces they come into contact with. This pressure is exerted uniformly in all directions within a container due to the constant, random motion of gas particles colliding with the walls.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0563.explanation: Initial rate = k[A]²[B]. New rate = k[2A]²[½B] = k × 4 × ½ × [A]²[B] = 2 × k[A]²[B]. Factor = 2.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0564.explanation: Molar mass ZnS = 65.4+32 = 97.4 g/mol. Moles ZnS = 35.5/97.4 = 0.3645 mol. From stoichiometry, 2 mol ZnS → 2 mol SO₂, so theoretical moles SO₂ = 0.3645 mol. Molar mass SO₂ = 32+32=64 g/mol. Theoretical mass SO₂ = 0.3645 × 64 = 23.33 g. % yield = (17.3/23.33)×100% = 74.1% ≈ 74%. Option B is 74%.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0565.explanation: In option D, Zn is oxidized (0 to +2) and Cu²⁺ is reduced (+2 to 0). The other options are acid-base or precipitation reactions with no change in oxidation states.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0566.explanation: Balanced half-reactions: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O and Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻ (×5). Combined: MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O. Coefficient of Fe²⁺ is 5.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0567.explanation: A cation is formed when an atom loses one or more electrons, resulting in a net positive charge. An anion is formed when an atom gains one or more electrons, resulting in a net negative charge.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0568.explanation: An electrolytic cell uses an external electrical source to drive a non-spontaneous chemical reaction, thereby converting electrical energy into chemical energy.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0569.explanation: In a neutral atom, the number of protons equals the number of electrons. This balance results in a net charge of zero because the positive charges of the protons are exactly canceled by the negative charges of the electrons.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0570.explanation: Valence Bond Theory principles: Bond forms when atomic orbitals overlap, overlap leads to shared electron density, and greater overlap means stronger bond.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0571.explanation: Required magnesium for 0.252 mol Fe₂O₃ is 0.756 mol, less than available Mg, so Fe₂O₃ is limiting.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0572.explanation: Oxygen has the electron configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁴. The 2p subshell has three degenerate orbitals. According to Hund's rule, electrons occupy each orbital singly with parallel spins before pairing. With 4 electrons in the 2p subshell, one orbital is fully paired (2 electrons) and two orbitals contain one unpaired electron each, resulting in two unpaired electrons.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0573.explanation: ΔH°rxn = Σ ΔHf°(products) - Σ ΔHf°(reactants) = [2 × (-36)] - [0 + 31] = -72 - 31 = -103 kJ/mol.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0574.explanation:
The correct answer is D. trans-isomer.

In the context of geometric isomerism for alkenes, the prefix trans- (from Latin, meaning "across") is used when the identical groups—in this case, the two methyl ($-CH_3$) groups—are on opposite sides of the double bond.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0575.explanation: Alkanes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. For n=5, C₅H₁₂ fits this formula. C₃H₆ and C₂H₄ are alkenes (CₙH₂ₙ), and C₄H₈ could be an alkene or cycloalkane.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0576.explanation: Endothermic reactions absorb heat from the surroundings. The enthalpy of the products is greater than that of the reactants, so ΔH is positive.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0577.explanation: For a zero-order reaction, rate = k. Rate has units of M s⁻¹, so the units of k are also M s⁻¹.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0578.explanation: Louis de Broglie proposed that matter, including electrons, exhibits wave-like properties. He suggested that every particle has a wavelength related to its mass and velocity, expressed by the de Broglie relation λ = h/mv, extending wave-particle duality to matter.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0579.explanation: If heat is absorbed, the products have more stored (chemical potential) energy than the reactants.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0580.explanation: Molecularity is the number of molecules that collide in the rate-determining step. The equation shows X and Y reacting directly, so two molecules are involved: bimolecular.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0581.explanation: With N₂ as limiting reagent, 1 molecule of N₂ produces 2 molecules of NH₃ according to the balanced equation.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0582.explanation: When atoms have similar electronegativities, neither atom strongly attracts the bonding electrons away from the other. This leads to the sharing of electrons, which is the basis of covalent bonding.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0583.explanation: Copper is a metal with a 'sea' of delocalized electrons that are free to move and carry an electric current. Plastic, rubber, and wood are insulators because their electrons are tightly bound.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0584.explanation: ΔH_rxn = Σ ΔH_f°(products) - Σ ΔH_f°(reactants) = ΔH_f°(NH4Cl) - [ΔH_f°(NH3) + ΔH_f°(HCl)].

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0586.explanation: Rusting of iron involves the oxidation of iron (Fe → Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺) by oxygen. The other options are physical changes or acid-base reactions without change in oxidation states.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0587.explanation: Atomicity is the total number of atoms in a molecule. For H2SO4, there are 2 hydrogen atoms, 1 sulfur atom, and 4 oxygen atoms. The total is 2 + 1 + 4 = 7 atoms.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0588.explanation: Anions are negatively charged ions formed when atoms gain electrons. Nonmetallic atoms, typically found on the right side of the periodic table, tend to gain electrons to achieve a stable electron configuration, forming anions.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0590.explanation: Group I elements have very low electronegativity (they are electropositive). They readily lose their valence electron, not gain.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0592.explanation: The reaction requires more oxygen relative to ammonia. Available oxygen is insufficient for the amount of ammonia present, making O₂ the limiting reactant.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0593.explanation: For reaction 1: K₁ = [C][D]^(5/2) / [A][B]² = 4.0. The target reaction is the reverse of twice reaction 1. For reverse: K_rev = 1/K₁. For multiplying by 2: K = (1/K₁)² = (1/4)² = 1/16 = 0.0625 ≈ 0.063.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0594.explanation: ΔHᵣₓₙ = ΣnH_products - ΣmH_reactants. If H_products > H_reactants, ΔH is positive (endothermic). If H_products < H_reactants, ΔH is negative (exothermic).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0595.explanation: Without complete structures, a carboxylic acid contains the -COOH group (carbonyl with a hydroxyl attached). Option D likely represents this functional group.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0596.explanation: In the first stage of quantum theory development, the electron was treated as a particle. This was used to explain atomic spectra and assignment of electronic configurations.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0597.explanation: Chemical properties are primarily determined by the number and arrangement of valence electrons. Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons, leading to similar bonding behavior and reactivity.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0598.explanation: In an electrolytic cell, electrical energy is used to drive a non-spontaneous chemical reaction. The passage of electric current initiates (or forces) the chemical reaction to occur. Option B is also correct in meaning, but A is the direct description of what happens.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0599.explanation: Moles Ag⁺ = 0.0250 L × 0.366 M = 0.00915 mol. Reaction is 1:1, so moles NaCl needed = 0.00915 mol. Molar mass NaCl = 58.44 g/mol. Mass = 0.00915 × 58.44 = 0.535 g.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0600.explanation: Non-metals are located on the right-hand side of the periodic table (except hydrogen).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0601.explanation: If T is high, ΔS_surr is small, and system's entropy ΔS_sys dominates. If T is low, ΔS_surr is large, and exothermicity strongly drives spontaneity.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0602.explanation: Precision describes the reproducibility or repeatability of measurements. If multiple measurements of the same quantity are very close to each other, the measurements are said to be precise.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0603.explanation: Natural gas burns cleanly, produces fewer by-products, and releases less CO₂ than coal or petroleum.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0604.explanation: Gases have very low densities because the particles will space out to fill the container. The volume occupied is large compared to the mass of the gas, resulting in low density (mass per unit volume).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0605.explanation: In the reaction Mg + Cl2 → MgCl2, magnesium (a metal) loses electrons to form Mg2+ cations, and chlorine (a nonmetal) gains electrons to form Cl- anions. The electrostatic attraction between these oppositely charged ions forms the ionic compound magnesium chloride.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0606.explanation: The standard enthalpy of formation of liquid water is -285.8 kJ/mol.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0607.explanation: Atomicity is the total number of atoms in a molecule. For C9H8O4, the number of carbon atoms is 9, hydrogen atoms is 8, and oxygen atoms is 4. The sum is 9 + 8 + 4 = 21 atoms.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0608.explanation: 2.8 mol TiCl₄ requires 5.6 mol Mg (2.8 × 2). Since only 5.4 mol Mg is present, Mg is limiting and TiCl₄ is in excess.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0609.explanation: The formula Ca(H2PO4)2 contains 1 Ca atom, and inside the parentheses: 2 H atoms, 1 P atom, and 4 O atoms. The subscript '2' outside multiplies these: (H2PO4)2 gives 2*2=4 H atoms, 2*1=2 P atoms, and 2*4=8 O atoms. Total atoms = 1 Ca + 4 H + 2 P + 8 O = 15 atoms.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0611.explanation: Molar mass = 197.378 g/mol, mass of F = 57.00 g/mol. %F = 28.86%.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0612.explanation: Hess's Law: The overall ΔH for a reaction is the sum of ΔH values for any series of steps, regardless of the reaction pathway.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0614.explanation: If two or more atoms of different elements are chemically bound, the substance meets the definition of a molecule (two or more atoms bonded) and also the definition of a compound (two or more different elements bonded).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0616.explanation: To write chemical formulas: The charge on the cation becomes the subscript on the anion. The charge on the anion becomes the subscript on the cation. If these subscripts are not in the lowest whole-number ratio, divide them by the greatest common factor.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0617.explanation: An element is a pure substance composed of only one type of atom. A molecule is a neutral group of two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds, and these atoms may be of the same element or different elements.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0619.explanation: HCl is limiting, producing about 0.045 mol ZnCl₂, which corresponds to roughly 6.17 g.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0620.explanation: A crystalline solid is a substance whose constituents possess an orderly arrangement in a definite geometric pattern. Examples include sodium chloride, sugar, and diamond.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0621.explanation: Larger molecules (with greater molecular weight and more electrons) have larger electron clouds that are more easily polarized. This increased polarizability leads to stronger London dispersion forces, which require more energy to overcome, resulting in higher melting and boiling points.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0622.explanation: Ultraviolet (UV) light is a physical disinfection method that inactivates microorganisms by damaging their DNA. It does not introduce any chemical residues, so it leaves no taste or smell.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0623.explanation: Hess's Law is based on the fact that enthalpy is a state function, so energy change for any process is independent of the pathway or number of steps.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0624.explanation: In an electrolytic cell, the anode is connected to the positive terminal of the power supply, attracting anions and undergoing oxidation.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0625.explanation: John Dalton's atomic theory (early 1800s) stated that all atoms of a given element are identical in mass and properties, and atoms of different elements differ.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0626.explanation: Enthalpy change (ΔH) is a state function and depends on the initial and final states. The physical states (solid, liquid, gas) are part of defining that state, as they have different inherent enthalpies. A catalyst, activation energy, and reaction rate do not affect the overall ΔH.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0627.explanation: Hydrogen bonding requires a hydrogen atom covalently bonded to a small, highly electronegative atom (N, O, or F). This creates a strong dipole, allowing the partially positive hydrogen to be attracted to lone pairs on other electronegative atoms.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0628.explanation: The calorie (cal) is a non-SI unit of energy still widely used, especially in chemistry and nutrition.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0629.explanation: The modern standard for atomic mass is the carbon-12 atom. One atom of carbon-12 is assigned a mass of exactly 12 atomic mass units (u), and the masses of all other atoms are relative to this standard.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0630.explanation: Ionic bond strength depends on charge magnitude and distance between ions. Greater charge and smaller ionic radius lead to stronger bond.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0631.explanation: The standard sequence is: 1. Ask a question, 2. Form a hypothesis, 3. Test the hypothesis (experiment), 4. Analyze results, 5. Draw conclusions, 6. Communicate results.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0632.explanation: Balanced equation: 2C₂H₆ + 7O₂ → 4CO₂ + 6H₂O. The coefficient for O₂ is 7.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0633.explanation: A nonspontaneous process does not occur on its own and requires an input of energy or coupling to another process, like extracting iron from iron ore.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0634.explanation: Our knowledge of electronic structure is the result of major developments of twentieth century science called the quantum theory.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0635.explanation: Primary valence forces involve electron transfer or sharing and are responsible for holding atoms together in compounds and solids.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0636.explanation: Universe = System and Surroundings. The system is separated from the surrounding by a boundary.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0637.explanation: The arrangement of electrons in an atom is called its electronic structure. It includes the number of electrons an atom possesses, their distribution around the atom, and their energies.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0638.explanation: Covalent bond strength is 50-200 kJ/mole, while intermolecular forces are much weaker at 1-12 kJ/mole.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0639.explanation: Percentage composition of A = (mass of A in one mole / molar mass of compound) × 100 = (25 g / 100 g) × 100 = 25%.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0640.explanation: Ionic compounds conduct electricity when aqueous or molten because the ions are free to move. When solid, the ions are fixed in an ionic lattice so can't conduct electricity.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0641.explanation: Using $r = \frac{k \cdot q_1 \cdot q_2}{U}$, we have $r = \frac{(9 \times 10^9) \cdot (2 \times 10^{-4}) \cdot (4 \times 10^{-4})}{180}$. This simplifies to $r = \frac{720}{180} = 4.0 \text{ m}$.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0644.explanation: A tight group at the center of the target represents measurements that are both precise (close to each other) and accurate (close to the true value, the bullseye).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0645.explanation: A large electronegativity difference (> ~1.7) typically results in an ionic bond. A moderate difference results in a polar covalent bond.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0646.explanation: In chemistry, the most important potential energy is the electrostatic potential energy. It arises as a result of the interactions between charged particles.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0647.explanation: The Pauli exclusion principle states that no two electrons in the same atom may have the same set of n, l, ml, and ms quantum numbers.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0648.explanation: Reducing external pressure allows the gas particles to move further apart, causing the gas to expand.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0649.explanation: The balanced equation shows 4 mol HCl : 1 mol MnO₂. 5.2 mol HCl would require 1.3 mol MnO₂ (5.2/4). With 1.5 mol MnO₂ available, HCl is limiting. Amount of Cl₂ = 5.2 mol HCl × (1 mol Cl₂/4 mol HCl) = 1.3 mol.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0650.explanation: The Pauli exclusion principle states no two electrons in an atom can have the same set of four quantum numbers. Option D shows different l values (3 vs 2), so they are different orbitals; this does not violate Pauli. The question likely expects identification of a pair that violates, but all given pairs have either different m or different l. Option A and B are valid pairs in the same orbital with opposite spins. None clearly violate Pauli; there may be an error in the options. Option D has different l, so it's allowed.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0651.explanation: The question likely refers to Cl⁻ ions (common for such problems). Each formula unit of MgCl₂ contains 2 Cl⁻ ions. Moles of Cl⁻ ions = (5.0 × 10²³) / (6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹) ≈ 0.83 mol. Moles of MgCl₂ needed = 0.83 mol Cl⁻ / 2 = 0.415 mol. Molar mass of MgCl₂ ≈ 24.3 + (2 × 35.5) = 95.3 g/mol. Mass = 0.415 mol × 95.3 g/mol ≈ 39.5 g. However, if the question intends 5.0 x 10²³ Mg²⁺ ions, moles = 0.83 mol MgCl₂, mass ≈ 79.1 g, matching option B. The provided answer confirms B, so we assume the 'ions' are Mg²⁺ or the calculation is for the total ions in 0.83 mol of formula units.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0652.explanation: The standard enthalpy of formation for liquid water, ΔH_f°(H2O(l)), is -285.8 kJ/mol, often rounded to -286 kJ/mol.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0653.explanation: Surface tension results from the net inward force experienced by the molecules on the surface of a liquid. Molecules at the surface have fewer neighboring molecules to attract them, creating a tighter, more cohesive surface layer.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0654.explanation: According to the kinetic theory, the average kinetic energy of gas particles is directly proportional to the absolute temperature of the particles. As temperature increases, the particles move faster and have greater kinetic energy.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0655.explanation: A small amount of energy is used to promote one of the 2s electrons to the empty 2p orbital (as these have a similar energy) to give 4 unpaired electrons. The carbon atom is now in an excited state.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0656.explanation: SP3 is a very common hybridization (e.g., in methane, ammonia).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0657.explanation: When l = 1 (p subshell), there are 3 permissible values of ml: -1, 0, +1. This means there are three atomic orbitals associated with a p subshell: px, py, and pz.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0658.explanation: Dalton proposed that atoms of a given element are identical in size, mass and other properties.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0659.explanation: After determining H₂ as limiting reagent, nCH₃OH = 0.64356 mol H₂ × (1 mol CH₃OH/2 mol H₂) = 0.32178 mol. Mass = 0.32178 mol × 32.02 g/mol = 10.3 g.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0660.explanation: John Dalton's atomic theory included the idea that atoms of different elements combine in simple whole number ratios to form compounds, which is the basis of the law of definite proportions.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0661.explanation: Liquids expand when heated because the particles gain kinetic energy and move more vigorously. This increased motion allows particles to exist at greater distances from each other, while the intermolecular forces remain constant, resulting in an overall volume increase.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0662.explanation: Number of atoms = moles × Avogadro's number = 0.11 × 6.023 × 10²³ = 6.6 × 10²² atoms.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0663.explanation: Increasing the pressure favors the side with fewer moles of gas. The left side (N2 + 3H2) has 4 moles of gas, and the right side (2NH3) has 2 moles. Higher pressure will therefore shift the equilibrium to the right, producing more ammonia.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0664.explanation: Democritus and his teacher Leucippus are credited with the early philosophical concept of atoms (atomos) as indivisible particles that make up all matter.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0665.explanation: The percentage composition of carbon in ethanol is 52.13%.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0666.explanation: A polar covalent bond is a type of covalent bond in which electrons are shared unequally between atoms. This unequal sharing occurs when atoms have different electronegativities, creating partial positive and negative charges on the bonded atoms.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0667.explanation: Stoichiometry deals with the quantities of materials/substance consumed (reactants) and materials produced (products) in chemical reactions.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0669.explanation: Deposition is the reverse of sublimation (e.g., frost forming from water vapor).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0670.explanation: The term entropy was coined by Rudolph Clausius in the nineteenth century.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0671.explanation: Secondary valence forces are weak intermolecular forces that act between molecules or neutral atoms and are weaker than primary bonds.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0672.explanation: A compound is a substance composed of two or more different elements that are chemically bonded together in a fixed, definite proportion by mass. This composition is uniform throughout the sample.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0674.explanation: The overall order is the sum of the exponents in the rate law. Here, 1 (from [NO]) + 2 (from [O₂]²) = 3, so it is third order overall.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0675.explanation: Bond enthalpy (or bond dissociation energy) is the average energy required to break one mole of a specific type of bond in a gaseous molecule, producing gaseous fragments.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0676.explanation: The increasing positive charge (more protons) exerts a stronger attractive force on the electron cloud, pulling it in and decreasing the atomic radius.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0677.explanation: For an isothermal process (constant temperature), the change in entropy is equal to the heat that would be transferred if the process were reversible divided by the temperature: ΔS = q_rev / T.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0678.explanation: Metals, especially those on the left side and bottom of the table, have low ionization energies, making them prone to losing electrons and forming cations.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0679.explanation: The reaction produces 2 moles of HBr and releases 72 kJ. For 1 mole of HBr, the heat released is 72 kJ / 2 = 36 kJ.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0680.explanation: Electrons in the same shell (valence electrons) are poor at shielding each other from the nucleus. Therefore, as protons are added, the effective nuclear charge felt by valence electrons increases significantly.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0681.explanation: The percentage composition of an element in a compound is calculated by dividing the total mass of that element in one mole of the compound by the molar mass of the compound, then multiplying by 100%.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0682.explanation: A bomb calorimeter operates at constant volume, used for measuring heats of combustion.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0683.explanation: The reaction is spontaneous in the reverse direction. Liquid water is very stable; decomposition requires electrical energy (electrolysis). It is highly endothermic, and ΔG > 0 at room temperature. The reverse reaction (formation of water from H₂ and O₂) is spontaneous and strongly exothermic.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0684.explanation: Diamond to graphite is thermodynamically spontaneous because graphite is more stable, but it is kinetically extremely slow, so diamonds don't turn into graphite.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0685.explanation: Anecdotal evidence relies on personal accounts or isolated examples that are not gathered through controlled, systematic, and repeatable experiments, making it prone to bias and error.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0686.explanation: The layers of positive ions can slide past one another without disrupting the delocalized electron sea, allowing deformation without fracture.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0687.explanation: Periodicity refers to the repeating pattern of chemical and physical properties of elements when arranged by atomic number.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0688.explanation: In a copper-silver cell, copper is more easily oxidized, so it is the anode (written on the left). The notation is: anode | oxidized species || reduced species | cathode. Cu(s) | Cu²⁺(aq) || Ag⁺(aq) | Ag(s).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0689.explanation: Sulfates (SO42-) are soluble with the exception of sulfates formed with Ca2+, Sr2+, and Ba2+.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0690.explanation: The delocalized electrons can move freely through the metal lattice, carrying electric current.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0691.explanation: The formula CaCO3 contains 1 calcium atom, 1 carbon atom, and 3 oxygen atoms. The total number of atoms is 1 + 1 + 3 = 5.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0692.explanation: An equation of state defines the physical state of matter, allowing prediction of pressure if volume, temperature, and amount are known.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0693.explanation: The Aufbau principle states that electrons fill orbitals in order of increasing energy. The 4s orbital is lower in energy than 3d for neutral atoms, so it fills first.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0694.explanation: Absolute error = measured value - true value.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0696.explanation: Stronger bond leads to shorter bond length.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0697.explanation: If all the ions in a reaction are shown to be soluble, then no precipitation reaction occurs.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0698.explanation: Density = 2.456 g / 1.2 mL = 2.0467 g/mL. The volume (1.2 mL) has 2 significant figures, so the answer should have 2 significant figures: 2.0 g/mL.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0699.explanation: The amount of product in a chemical reaction is determined by the amount of limiting reagent.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0701.explanation: Solids are difficult to compress because of the lack of empty space between the particles.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0702.explanation: The structure is but-2-ene with two methyl groups on the same side of the double bond. In the Z (from German 'zusammen', meaning together) isomer, the higher priority groups (both CH₃) are on the same side.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0703.explanation: An atom is the basic unit of a chemical element. It is the smallest particle of an element that retains the properties of that element and is a fundamental building block of all matter.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0704.explanation: With ΔH negative (favorable) and ΔS negative (unfavorable), spontaneity depends on temperature. The equation ΔG = ΔH - TΔS shows that at low temperatures, the favorable ΔH term dominates, making ΔG negative. At high temperatures, the unfavorable -TΔS term becomes too large.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0705.explanation: Both 2s and 4s orbitals have l = 0 (s orbital) but differ in their principal quantum number n. The principal quantum number (n = 2 for 2s and n = 4 for 4s) distinguishes these orbitals, indicating that the 4s electron occupies a higher energy level and is on average farther from the nucleus.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0706.explanation: AgNO₃ and NaI react to form AgI, which is insoluble in water (a yellow precipitate). The other pairs would form products that are all soluble.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0707.explanation: All real processes are irreversible. Reversible processes are ideal and spontaneous processes are always irreversible.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0710.explanation: Standard molar entropy (S°) is the entropy of 1 mole of a substance in its standard state at a specified temperature (usually 298 K). Units: J·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0711.explanation: The structure of carbocation is trigonal planar. The unhybridized p orbital remains empty and stands perpendicular to the plane.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0712.explanation: A combination reaction is sometimes called a synthesis reaction. It follows the general form A+B→AB.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0713.explanation: 345 cm has 3 sig figs. 6.050 m has 4 sig figs (trailing zero after decimal counts). 1.310 × 10²² has 4 sig figs. 0.00134 m has 3 sig figs (leading zeros don't count).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0714.explanation: Iron (Fe) goes from oxidation state 0 to +2, losing electrons. Therefore, Fe is oxidized.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0715.explanation: Democritus proposed that atoms are indivisible and differ in shape, size, and arrangement, accounting for different properties of matter.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0716.explanation: The mathematical statement of the first law for a closed system is ΔU = q + w, where q is heat added to the system and w is work done on the system.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0717.explanation: In ethylene, the remaining sp² hybrid orbitals of each carbon overlap with each other along the axis to form C-C sigma bond.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0718.explanation: °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32 = (23.5 × 1.8) + 32 = 42.3 + 32 = 74.3 °F. None match exactly. 71.3 would be 21.8°C. uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0719.explanation: A scientific theory is a well-substantiated explanation of some aspect of the natural world, but it begins as a tentative hypothesis. The correct description here is that it is a tentative statement proposing a possible explanation.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0720.explanation: In a chemical equation, the substances written on the left side of the arrow are the starting materials, which are called the reactants.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0721.explanation: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation for a phenomenon that must be testable through experimentation or observation.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0722.explanation: At equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates, so neither has stopped. There is no net change in concentrations.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0723.explanation: Nitrogen (N≡N) has bond order 3, making it a very strong bond.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0725.explanation: The magnetic quantum number (ml) designates the specific orbital within a subshell. Orbitals within a given subshell differ in their orientations in space but not in their energies.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0726.explanation: The subscripts in a chemical formula define the compound's identity (e.g., H₂O vs H₂O₂). Changing them would change the substance itself. To balance an equation, only the coefficients (the numbers in front of formulas) can be adjusted.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0727.explanation: Bond order is the number of shared electron pairs between two atoms.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0728.explanation: Entropy S = k ln Ω = 1.38×10⁻²³ × ln(500). Option C correctly represents this.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0729.explanation: Covalent bonds form when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0730.explanation: Phosphorus has the electron configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p³. The 3p subshell has three degenerate orbitals. With three electrons in the 3p subshell, Hund's rule dictates that each electron occupies a separate orbital with parallel spins, resulting in three unpaired electrons.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0733.explanation: ΔU = q + w. Releases heat: q = -12.4 J. Does work on surroundings: w = -4.2 J (work done by system is negative). ΔU = -12.4 + (-4.2) = -16.6 J.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0734.explanation: Proteins, like carbohydrates, provide about 4 kcal of metabolizable energy per gram.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0735.explanation: In a homogeneous mixture, the components are uniformly distributed and cannot be visually distinguished. Heterogeneous mixtures have visible distinct components.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0736.explanation: Particles in a gas are far apart and move at high speeds with the highest kinetic energy. Liquids have less, solids have the least.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0737.explanation: At equilibrium, the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal, so the net change in the concentrations of reactants and products is zero. This means their concentrations become constant, though not necessarily equal to each other.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0738.explanation: From the balanced equation, 2 moles of NO react with 1 mole of O₂ to produce 2 moles of NO₂. uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0739.explanation: 0.252 mol Fe₂O₃ produces twice as many moles of Fe (0.504 mol). Multiplying by molar mass gives about 28.2 g.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0740.explanation: Bohr theory explained only spherical orbits. There was no explanation for elliptical orbits.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0741.explanation: Electrons are released at the anode (oxidation) and travel through the external circuit to the cathode (reduction).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0742.explanation: Most decomposition reactions require an input of energy in the form of heat, light, or electricity to split the compound into simpler products.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0743.explanation: Carbon and hydrogen have similar electronegativity values (C = 2.55, H = 2.20), so the C-H bond is considered essentially non-polar.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0744.explanation: In an exothermic reaction, less energy is needed to break bonds in the reactants than is released when new bonds form in the products.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0745.explanation: A displacement/replacement/metathesis reaction is a type of reaction in which part of one reactant is replaced by another reactant. It takes place when a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal. It's represented as AB + C → AC + B.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0746.explanation: An open system can exchange both matter and energy with its surroundings. A closed system exchanges only energy, and an isolated system exchanges neither.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0748.explanation: Liquids have a fixed volume because the particles are close together and have significant attractive forces that maintain a constant volume. However, they take the shape of their container because the particles can move past each other and are not held in fixed positions.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0750.explanation: Scientific laws describe observed patterns or relationships (often mathematically), while theories provide explanatory frameworks for why those phenomena occur.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0751.explanation: CaCO3 (calcium carbonate) contains the polyatomic ion CO32- (carbonate). NaCl, MgO, and FeS are ionic compounds composed of monatomic ions only.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0752.explanation: Each period ends with a noble gas (inert gas), which has a full valence shell.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0753.explanation: Sodium (2,8,1) has one electron more than a stable noble gas structure (2,8). By losing that electron, it achieves a stable electron configuration similar to neon, forming a Na⁺ cation.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0754.explanation: An electrolytic cell uses an external source of electrical energy to force a non-spontaneous redox reaction to occur, converting electrical energy into chemical energy.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0756.explanation: The Third Law of Thermodynamics states that the entropy of a perfect crystal at absolute zero (0 Kelvin) is zero. This provides an absolute reference point for determining entropy values.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0757.explanation: In an exothermic process, heat is released (q < 0). Heat flows from the system to the surroundings.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0759.explanation: Using Boyle's Law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, 100 × 400 = 200 × V₂, V₂ = 200 cm³.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0760.explanation: During charging of a lead-acid battery, lead sulfate is reduced to lead at the cathode. The other options involve oxidation reactions or are not solely reduction.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0762.explanation: Van der Waals forces are weak attractions between neutral molecules.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0763.explanation: Absolute error = |observed value - true value|. Relative error is this divided by the true value.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0764.explanation: At higher pressures, real gas behavior deviates from ideal gas laws due to molecular interactions.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0765.explanation: Atoms become ions with electron configurations matching the nearest noble gas, which is particularly stable.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0766.explanation: 8.314 has 4 sig figs, 310 has 3 sig figs (or ambiguous), 96485 has 5 sig figs. uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0767.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element on the Pauling scale (assigned a value of 4.0).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0768.explanation: From Boltzmann's equation, S = k ln W = k ln 1 = 0, providing an absolute reference point for all entropy measurements.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0769.explanation: Bohr assumed that the prevailing laws of physics were inadequate to describe atoms and that energies are quantized (as Planck proposed).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0770.explanation: The notes provide the answer as 0.60 g NO for this reaction.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0771.explanation: In a negatively charged carbon, three of the sp³ hybrid orbitals overlap with the s orbital of H and the fourth sp³ orbital holds the non-bonding electron pair.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0772.explanation: Types of covalent bonds include single bond (1 shared pair), double bond (2 shared pairs), and triple bond (3 shared pairs).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0774.explanation: The change in entropy for a process is ΔS = k ln W_final - k ln W_initial = k ln (W_final / W_initial).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0775.explanation: The half-life of a reaction is the time it takes for the reactant concentration to decrease by half. For a first-order reaction, this value is constant, so if it is 50% complete in 30 minutes, the half-life is 30 minutes.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0776.explanation: Copper atom (Cu) has the configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹. To form Cu²⁺, the atom loses two electrons. The first electron is removed from the 4s orbital, and the second electron is removed from the 3d orbital, resulting in the configuration [Ar] 3d⁹.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0777.explanation: Ethyne (acetylene) is the smallest and most polarizable hydrocarbon among the options. Its triple bond and acidic hydrogen allow for weak dipole interactions and hydrogen bonding with water, giving it slightly higher solubility than other simple hydrocarbons.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0778.explanation: The rate constant k depends only on temperature and activation energy (and presence of a catalyst). Changing concentrations does not affect k.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0779.explanation: The notes use 28.01 g/mol as the molar mass of carbon monoxide.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0780.explanation: The concept of hybridization was first proposed by Linus Pauling in 1931.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0781.explanation: The valence shell is the outermost electron shell. Elements in a group have the same valence electron configuration, dictating their chemistry.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0782.explanation: Entropy increases when temperature increases (more microstates), volume increases (more space to move), number of independently moving molecules increases, and molecular complexity increases (more vibrational and rotational modes).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0783.explanation: In an ideal calorimeter (isolated system), the heat released by one part of the system equals the heat absorbed by another.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0784.explanation: All measurements that involve a numerical answer involve an error. The error could be from the instrument used or as a result of personal error.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0785.explanation: Groups IA, IIA, VIIA, and VIIIA are known as alkali metals, the alkaline-earth metals, the halogens, and noble gases respectively.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0786.explanation: A balanced chemical equation is fundamental to stoichiometry. It provides the correct mole ratios between reactants and products, which are essential for all subsequent calculations.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0787.explanation: The most common type of work encountered in chemistry is pressure-volume work, given by w = -PΔV. The negative sign shows that the system is doing work.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0788.explanation: Standard molar entropy has units of J·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0789.explanation: Moles of CO₃²⁻ = moles of CaCO₃ = 4.86 mol. Molar mass CO₃²⁻ = 12 + 48 = 60 g/mol. Mass = 4.86 × 60 = 291.6 g ≈ 292 g.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0790.explanation: The notes provide the answer as 0.54 g H₂O for this reaction.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0791.explanation: Niels Bohr's model proposed that electrons travel in specific, fixed circular paths or orbits (energy levels) around the nucleus, and they can only gain or lose energy by jumping between these levels.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0792.explanation: The formula Fe(OH)3 contains 1 Fe atom, and within (OH)3: 3 O atoms and 3 H atoms. Total atoms = 1 + 3 + 3 = 7 atoms.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0793.explanation: The Bohr model could not explain the uncertainty principle of Heisenberg.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0794.explanation: In explaining the line spectrum of hydrogen, Bohr started with Rutherford's idea by assuming that electrons move in circular orbits around the nucleus.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0795.explanation: Energy must be supplied to overcome the electrostatic attraction between the electron and the nucleus, so ionization is endothermic.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0796.explanation: A polar covalent bond involves unequal sharing of electrons due to a difference in electronegativity between the bonded atoms.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0797.explanation: Van der Waals forces include (a) Dipole-Dipole Interaction occurring between polar molecules, and (b) London Dispersion Forces present in all molecules due to temporary dipoles.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0798.explanation: The ratio of volumes (base:acid) is 30:20 = 3:2. If concentrations are equal, the mole ratio is 3:2. The question likely asks for the base:acid ratio, which is 3:2.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0799.explanation: Moving down a group, atomic radius increases, leading to decreased nuclear attraction on valence electrons. Both ionization energy and electronegativity decrease.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0800.explanation: When two atoms approach: attractive forces dominate at long distance, repulsive forces dominate at very short distance, and equilibrium bond distance occurs at minimum potential energy.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0801.explanation: Brittleness is not a property of metals; metals are typically malleable and ductile. Metals have high melting and boiling points, conduct electricity well due to delocalized electrons, and can be shaped without breaking.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0802.explanation: William Crookes, an English physicist, is credited with coining the term 'cathode' during his work with cathode rays in discharge tubes. Faraday is known for electrolysis laws, Thompson for the electron, Soddy for radioactivity.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0803.explanation: Iodine (I₂) is a solid at room temperature that readily sublimes, producing a purple vapor. The other substances do not sublime under these conditions.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0804.explanation: When solids are heated, particles gain kinetic energy and vibrate more strongly. Attractive forces weaken in comparison to particle energy, and particles become free to move around.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0805.explanation: Chemical bonds are the attractive forces that bind atoms together within molecules or crystalline solids. Intermolecular forces are weaker attractions that occur between neighboring molecules. Covalent bond strengths typically range from 50-200 kJ/mole, while intermolecular forces range from 1-12 kJ/mole.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0806.explanation: Gases expand to fill their container, taking both its shape and volume.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0807.explanation: Endothermic processes absorb heat from the surroundings. Evaporation (or vaporization) requires heat input to overcome intermolecular forces and convert a liquid to a gas.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0808.explanation: The four types of crystalline solids are ionic solids, molecular solids, network covalent solids, and metallic solids.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0810.explanation: Chromium has an anomalous configuration: [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹. This half-filled d subshell provides extra stability. The expected configuration would be 3d⁴ 4s².

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0811.explanation: An anion is a negative ion, formed when an atom gains electrons.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0812.explanation: The formation of 1 mol H₂O(l) releases 286 kJ. The decomposition of 2 mol H₂O(l) is the reverse of the formation of 2 mol H₂O(l). ΔH°rxn = -2 × (-286) = +572 kJ.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0813.explanation: Internal energy (U) is the sum of all kinetic and potential energies of the particles that make up a system. It is a state function.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0814.explanation: Work is defined as the transfer of energy that results in motion against an opposing force (force × distance). Heat is energy transfer due to temperature difference.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0815.explanation: Moles of CH₄ = 4.50/16 = 0.281 mol. Heat released = 0.281 mol × (-890 kJ/mol) = -250 kJ.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0816.explanation: Double displacement reactions are reactions in which ions are exchanged between two reactants forming new compounds. Cations and anions in the reactants switch partners to form products like trade by barter. Its general form is AB + CD → AD + CB.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0817.explanation: For a closed system, the First Law is expressed as ΔU = q + w.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0818.explanation: Plasma contains free-moving ions and electrons, making it electrically conductive. It is typically formed at very high temperatures or under strong electromagnetic fields.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0819.explanation: The reaction shows 2 mol H₂ (4.0 g) produces 571.6 kJ. 4.0 g H₂ = 2 mol (since molar mass H₂ = 2 g/mol). Thus, heat released = 571.6 kJ.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0820.explanation: Phosphorus exists as a tetra-atomic molecule with the formula P4, meaning each molecule contains four phosphorus atoms. Therefore, its atomicity is 4.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0821.explanation: The three main types of chemical bonds are ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding. Ionic bonding involves electron transfer, covalent bonding involves electron sharing, and metallic bonding involves delocalized electrons shared across metal atoms.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0822.explanation: Effective hydrogen bonding requires hydrogen to be bonded to a small, highly electronegative atom like N, O, or F. High electronegativity creates a strong dipole, and small size allows the hydrogen to approach closely for a strong attraction.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0823.explanation: The number of neutrons in an atom is calculated by subtracting the atomic number from the mass number. For uranium-235, mass number = 235 and atomic number = 92. Number of neutrons = 235 - 92 = 143.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0824.explanation: Examples of spontaneous processes include gas expanding into a vacuum, a book falling, a ball rolling downhill, and iron rusting in air.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0825.explanation: ΔU > 0 means the system gains energy. ΔU < 0 means the system loses energy.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0826.explanation: Mg(OH)2 has 1 Mg atom, 2 O atoms, and 2 H atoms, totaling 5 atoms. CO2 has 3 atoms, CH4 has 5 atoms (making it also correct), and H2O2 has 4 atoms. Since multiple options could have atomicity 5, the design requires selecting one valid example; Mg(OH)2 is a valid compound with atomicity 5.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0827.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its motion.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0828.explanation: sp hybridization involves the mixing of one s and one p orbital, resulting in two linear hybrid orbitals oriented 180° apart. This gives a bond angle of 180°.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0829.explanation: Atomicity of a substance is the total number of atoms present in each stable molecule of the substance.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0830.explanation: The rows of the table are called periods, and the columns are called groups. Some groups have names such as halogens, noble gases, or alkali metals.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0831.explanation: When Mg2+ combines with O2-, the formula is MgO, not Mg2O2, because the subscripts are divided by the greatest common factor to get the lowest whole-number ratio.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0832.explanation: Observations themselves are not 'tested'; they are the data collected. Hypotheses and theories are tested. 'Averagely tested' is not a meaningful phrase in the context of scientific observation.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0833.explanation: The ionic bonding in MgO is stronger because Mg²⁺ attracts O²⁻ with a 2+ charge interacting with a 2- charge. In NaCl, Na⁺ attracts Cl⁻ with only 1+ and 1- charges. The greater the charges on the ions, the stronger the electrostatic attraction between them.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0834.explanation: CaF₂(s) ⇌ Ca²⁺(aq) + 2F⁻(aq). If solubility s = 2.0×10⁻⁴ M, then [Ca²⁺] = s, [F⁻] = 2s. Ksp = [Ca²⁺][F⁻]² = s × (2s)² = 4s³ = 4 × (2.0×10⁻⁴)³ = 4 × 8.0×10⁻¹² = 3.2×10⁻¹¹.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0835.explanation: q = mCΔT = 200 × 4.18 × 6 = 5016 J = 5.02 kJ. Energy per gram = 5.02 kJ / 2 g = 2.51 kJ/g.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0836.explanation: Heat (q) is the transfer of thermal energy between a system and its surroundings due to a temperature gradient. Work is energy transfer due to a force acting through a distance.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0837.explanation: Thomson regarded the atom as containing a large number of smaller bodies which he called corpuscles. The corpuscles are the electrons.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0838.explanation: Internal energy, U, of a system is the total kinetic and potential energy possessed as a result of the spatial arrangement of its constituent atoms or molecules.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0839.explanation: The products listed in the reaction are CO₂, H₂O, and Na₃C₆H₅O₇. Therefore, along with CO₂, water (H₂O) is also produced.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0840.explanation: The First Law states that neither matter nor energy can be created or destroyed, only transferred or transformed. The total energy of an isolated system remains constant. Mathematically, ΔU = q + w.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0841.explanation: Fats have an average fuel value of 38 kJ/g. They release more than twice the energy per gram than carbohydrates or proteins due to high proportion of C-H bonds and low oxygen content.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0842.explanation: The order of ease of compression is: gas > liquid > solid. Gases are easily compressed because of the space between particles.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0843.explanation: Increase in temperature increases the kinetic energy of gas particles, leading to more frequent and forceful collisions with the container walls.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0844.explanation: Democritus, an ancient Greek philosopher, proposed that matter was made of small, uncuttable particles. He named these particles 'atomos,' which is Greek for 'indivisible' or 'not able to be cut.'

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0845.explanation: When ΔH is negative and ΔS is negative, ΔG = ΔH - TΔS becomes negative only at low temperatures where the TΔS term is small. Thus, the reaction is spontaneous at low temperatures.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0846.explanation: Gases exert pressure in all directions because their particles are in constant, random, rapid motion. They collide with the walls of their container from all directions, resulting in uniform pressure throughout.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0847.explanation: Ionic bonds form when valence electrons are transferred from metal atoms to nonmetal atoms. This transfer results in the formation of positively charged cations (from the metal) and negatively charged anions (from the nonmetal), which are held together by electrostatic attraction.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0848.explanation: A molecule consists of two or more atoms of the same element, or different elements, that are chemically bound together.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0851.explanation: The question seems to be for C₂H₅F? Given formula is C₂H₅Cl, but asking for %F. Likely intended compound is C₂H₅F. Molar mass C₂H₅F = (2×12) + (5×1) + 19 = 24+5+19 = 48 g/mol. %F = (19/48)×100 = 39.6%. Not matching options. For C₂H₅Cl, %Cl = (35.5/64.5)×100 = 55.0%. None match. The closest option is 29.5%.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0852.explanation: Nuclear energy comes from the conversion of mass into energy, described by Einstein's equation E = mc², where c is the speed of light (3.0 × 10⁸ m/s).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0853.explanation: 0.00476 has 3 sig figs (the leading zeros are not significant; 4,7,6 are). 0.4760 has 4, 4760 is ambiguous (could be 3 or 4, but typically 3 if no decimal), 0.004410 has 4.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0854.explanation: From the balanced equation, the mole ratio of NO to NO₂ is 2:2, which simplifies to 1:1. Therefore, moles of NO₂ produced = moles of NO reacted = 0.866 mol.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0855.explanation: For both changes to decrease products: (i) Increasing pressure favors side with fewer gas moles. (ii) Decreasing temperature favors exothermic direction (negative ΔH). For option D: N₂O₄ ⇌ 2NO₂, Δn = +1, so increased pressure favors reactants (decrease products). ΔH is positive (endothermic), so decreasing temperature favors reactants (decrease products). Both changes decrease products.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0856.explanation: The law of conservation of mass states that matter cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction, which allows us to balance chemical equations so that the same number of atoms of each element appear on both sides.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0857.explanation: Gases have particles that are widely spaced and scattered, undergo random and rapid motion, and have negligible forces of attraction between them. These characteristics explain the compressibility, expansibility, and low density of gases.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0858.explanation: Total volume = 25.0 mL + 25.0 mL = 50.0 mL. With density 1.00 g/mL, mass = 50.0 g.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0859.explanation: The particles of liquids move rapidly in all directions.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0860.explanation: Calorimetry is the science of measuring heat flow in chemical or physical processes. The instrument used is called a calorimeter.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0861.explanation: Precision refers to the reproducibility of measurements (how close they are to each other). Accuracy refers to how close a measurement is to the true value. If they are close to each other but far from the true value, they are precise but not accurate.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0862.explanation: When ΔH is positive and ΔS is positive, ΔG = ΔH - TΔS becomes negative only at high temperatures where the TΔS term dominates. Thus, the reaction is spontaneous at high temperatures.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0863.explanation: Air in a syringe can be compressed by pushing the plunger inward, demonstrating the compressibility of gases.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0864.explanation: Hydrogen bonding is a relatively strong intermolecular force. Extra energy is required to overcome these forces during vaporization, leading to higher boiling points for compounds that exhibit hydrogen bonding, such as ethanol and water.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0865.explanation: Molar mass is defined as the mass of one mole of a substance. Its common unit in chemistry is grams per mole (g/mol).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0866.explanation: The formula HCl consists of one hydrogen atom and one chlorine atom. The total number of atoms is 1 + 1 = 2. Therefore, its atomicity is 2.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0867.explanation: H2 (hydrogen gas) and CH4 (methane) are classic examples of covalent molecules.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0868.explanation: For a zero-order reaction with respect to a reactant, the rate does not change as the concentration of that reactant changes. The rate is independent of its concentration.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0869.explanation: Water (H₂O) has hydrogen atoms covalently bonded to a highly electronegative oxygen atom. This allows the hydrogen atoms to form hydrogen bonds with lone pairs on the oxygen atoms of neighboring water molecules.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0870.explanation: A scientific theory is not a wild guess; it is a well-substantiated explanation supported by a large body of evidence and repeated testing.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0871.explanation: If two molecules are of comparable size and shape, dipole-dipole interactions will likely be the dominating force. If one molecule is much larger than another, dispersion forces will likely determine its physical properties.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0872.explanation: NH₃ accepts a proton to form NH₄⁺. NH₄⁺ is the conjugate acid of NH₃.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0873.explanation: Both solutions have the same concentration (0.200 M). Mixing them does not change the concentration; it remains 0.200 M.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0874.explanation: Second ionization energy is the energy to remove a second electron. Sodium (Na) has an electron configuration of [Ne]3s¹. After removing the first electron, it achieves the stable, full-shell configuration of neon ([Ne]). Removing a second electron from this very stable configuration requires a huge amount of energy, giving sodium a very high second ionization energy.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0875.explanation: Electroplating with a less active metal would create a galvanic cell where the more active metal (iron) would corrode preferentially if the coating is scratched. Cathodic protection involves coating with a more active metal like zinc (galvanizing).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0876.explanation: Plasma is the most common state of matter in the universe, making up stars and interstellar space.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0877.explanation: The percentage composition of hydrogen in ethanol is 13.15%.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0878.explanation: A microstate refers to a specific arrangement or configuration of particles in a system, including their positions and energy levels at a given instant.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0879.explanation: Balanced equation: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂. Coefficient of NO₂ is 4.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0880.explanation: Spontaneity does not indicate speed; a reaction can be spontaneous but slow, like the conversion of diamond to graphite.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0881.explanation: John Dalton proposed the first modern atomic theory in the early 1800s, which stated that atoms are indivisible and indestructible particles.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0882.explanation: SP3: one s orbital + three p orbitals. s character = 1/4 = 25%. p character = 3/4 = 75%.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0883.explanation: Ionic compounds are held together by strong electrostatic attractions between the positively charged cations and negatively charged anions. These attractions are the ionic bonds that give ionic compounds their characteristic properties.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0884.explanation: Problems with coal include air pollution (sulfur converted to SO₂), mining hazards, and high transportation costs.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0885.explanation: Elements in their standard states (e.g., O2(g), C(graphite), Na(s)) are assigned ΔH_f° = 0 as a reference point.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0886.explanation: The carbon atom in methyl radical is also sp² hybridised. The unpaired electron is in the p orbital.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0887.explanation: While electrons repel each other, they occasionally wind up on the same side of the atom. At that instant, the helium atom is polar, with an excess of electrons on one side and a shortage on the other side.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0888.explanation: [H⁺] = 10⁻³·³⁸ = 4.17 × 10⁻⁴ M. For a weak acid HA ⇌ H⁺ + A⁻, Kₐ = [H⁺]² / (C - [H⁺]) = (4.17 × 10⁻⁴)² / (0.01 - 0.000417) = (1.74 × 10⁻⁷) / (0.009583) = 1.82 × 10⁻⁵. The provided answer key says 1.67 × 10⁻³, which is inconsistent with the calculation. The correct Kₐ for ethanoic acid is ~1.8 × 10⁻⁵.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0889.explanation: Dalton proposed that atoms are indivisible, indestructible spheres. Later discoveries showed atoms are divisible into subatomic particles.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0890.explanation: Anecdotal evidence is based on personal accounts or isolated examples that have not been subjected to rigorous, repeatable testing by other competent investigators.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0891.explanation: Evaporation is a phase change from liquid to gas, which does not alter the chemical composition of water (H₂O). The other options involve chemical reactions forming new substances.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0892.explanation: Benzene is the limiting reagent and theoretical yield is about 60 g. Actual yield 56.7 g gives approximately 94.5% yield.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0893.explanation: At constant temperature and pressure, ΔS_surr = -ΔH_sys / T. The sign depends on direction of heat flow and magnitude depends on temperature.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0894.explanation: As n increases, the electron spends more time farther from the nucleus.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0895.explanation: Heat is defined as the transfer of thermal energy due to a temperature difference between a system and its surroundings.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0896.explanation: Photosynthesis converts solar energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0897.explanation: When two objects of different temperatures are placed in contact, heat is transferred until thermal equilibrium. HeatLost = HeatGained.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0898.explanation: Covalent bonding involves the sharing of electron pairs between atoms. This type of bonding is most common between nonmetal atoms that have similar electronegativities, as neither atom completely transfers its electrons to the other.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0899.explanation: Deposition is the process by which a gas changes directly into a solid without passing through the liquid state. For example, iodine vapor on cooling solidifies directly to iodine crystals, demonstrating deposition.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0900.explanation: The kinetic theory of matter states that matter is made of tiny particles which are in constant random motion.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0901.explanation: The three primary types of strong chemical bonds are ionic, covalent, and metallic.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0902.explanation: The order of ease of compression is gas > liquid > solid. Gases are most easily compressed due to large intermolecular spaces, liquids are moderately compressible, and solids are very difficult to compress because particles are already closely packed.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0903.explanation: Democritus's atomic theory was philosophical and not based on experimental evidence or the scientific method, which was a major criticism. It was later refined by Dalton with experimental support.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0905.explanation: Balanced equation: Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) + Na₂S(aq) → PbS(s) + 2NaNO₃(aq). Moles Pb(NO₃)₂ = (0.2578 L)(0.0468 mol/L) = 0.01206 mol. Moles Na₂S = (0.156 L)(0.095 mol/L) = 0.01482 mol. Pb(NO₃)₂ is the limiting reactant. Moles PbS = 0.01206 mol. Mass PbS = 0.01206 × (207 + 32) = 0.01206 × 239 = 2.882 g ≈ 2.88 g.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0906.explanation: In an endothermic process, the system gains heat from the surroundings, so q > 0.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0907.explanation: Balanced equation: 2KOH + H₂SO₄ → K₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Moles H₂SO₄ = 0.01500 L × 0.100 M = 0.001500 mol. Moles KOH = 2 × 0.001500 = 0.003000 mol. Concentration KOH = 0.003000 mol / 0.02000 L = 0.150 M.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0909.explanation: Oxidation is defined as the loss of electrons, which results in an increase in the oxidation number of an element.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0910.explanation: Solids expand on heating due to the increased energy of the particles at higher temperatures. This allows the particles to exist at greater distances from each other because the intermolecular forces are constant.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0911.explanation: Acetates (C2H3O2-), nitrates (NO3-), and perchlorates (ClO4-) are soluble according to the solubility rules.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0912.explanation: The standard enthalpy of formation is the enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is formed from its constituent elements in their standard states. Forming water from hydrogen and oxygen gas fits this definition.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0913.explanation: Across a period, nuclear charge increases while shielding remains relatively constant, pulling electrons closer and decreasing atomic radius.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0914.explanation: The 4s orbital fills before 3d (except for certain exceptions after filling). Statement D is incorrect.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0915.explanation: Across a period, effective nuclear charge increases and atomic size decreases, making atoms better at attracting electrons, so electronegativity increases.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0916.explanation: The mole ratio of C₃H₈ to O₂ is 1:5. Therefore, for 2 moles of C₃H₈, the moles of O₂ required are 2 × 5 = 10 moles.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0917.explanation: Initial [N₂O₄] = 1 M. At equilibrium: [N₂O₄] = (1-x) M, [NO₂] = 2x M. Kc = [NO₂]²/[N₂O₄] = (2x)²/(1-x) = 4x²/(1-x).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0918.explanation: Covalent bonding arises from overlap of atomic orbitals. Two types are Sigma (σ) bond – head-on overlap, and Pi (π) bond – sidewise overlap.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0919.explanation: Bonds broken: 1 H-H (436) + 1 Cl-Cl (243) = 679 kJ. Bonds formed: 2 H-Cl (2 × 431 = 862 kJ). ΔH = 679 - 862 = -183 kJ.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0920.explanation: Max Planck, a German physicist, proposed in 1900 that energy is quantized, meaning atoms can only release or absorb energy in discrete packets called quanta. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1918 for this work, which laid the foundation for quantum theory.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0921.explanation: A calorie is defined as the amount of energy required to raise the temperature of water from 14.5°C to 15.5°C. 1 cal = 4.184 J.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0922.explanation: Chromium and copper exhibit anomalous electron configurations due to the closeness of the 3d and 4s orbital energies. Chromium prefers [Ar] 4s¹ 3d⁵ rather than [Ar] 4s² 3d⁴, and copper prefers [Ar] 4s¹ 3d¹⁰ rather than [Ar] 4s² 3d⁹. These configurations provide extra stability from half-filled or fully filled d subshells.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0923.explanation: Initial rate = k[A][B]². If [B] doubles, new rate = k[A](2B)² = k[A] × 4[B]² = 4 × k[A][B]². Factor = 4.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0924.explanation: The distinctive features of solids are: they have a definite shape, they are rigid and hard, and they have fixed volume.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0925.explanation: The standard sequence is: make an observation, form a hypothesis, conduct experiments, analyze data, and develop a theory based on supported hypotheses.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0926.explanation: H₂O molecules have polar covalent bonds between O and H. These polar molecules are attracted to each other via intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0927.explanation: The word thermodynamics comes from Greek: 'therme' means heat and 'dynamis' means power.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0928.explanation: According to the kinetic molecular theory, gas particles are separated by large distances relative to their size. The empty space allows them to be compressed into a smaller volume.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0929.explanation: Water donates a proton to NH₃, forming NH₄⁺ and OH⁻. Thus, H₂O is the acid (proton donor).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0930.explanation: Processes that are spontaneous in one direction are nonspontaneous in the opposite direction.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0931.explanation: This is the standard enthalpy of formation of CO(g), which is -110.5 kJ/mol. In kcal (1 kcal ≈ 4.184 kJ), this is approximately -26.4 kcal/mol.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0932.explanation: The tetrahedral geometry of SP3 hybrid orbitals results in bond angles of approximately 109.5°.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0933.explanation: The Bohr model was successful in explaining the hydrogen atom but failed for atoms with more than one electron, such as helium and lithium. It also could not explain elliptical orbits or the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0934.explanation: Matter possesses kinetic energy due to the motion of the particles.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0935.explanation: Dalton's Atomic Theory states that matter is composed of extremely small indivisible particles called atoms.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0937.explanation: Democritus proposed that if we continue to cut matter, a time comes when we eventually end up with the 'uncuttable' particle, which he named the atom.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0938.explanation: For a process at constant pressure, the change in enthalpy (ΔH) is equal to the heat exchanged (q_p).

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0939.explanation: Ionic compounds form crystals that are composed of oppositely charged ions: a positively charged cation and a negatively charged anion.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0940.explanation: The formula C6H12O6 contains 6 carbon atoms, 12 hydrogen atoms, and 6 oxygen atoms. The total number of atoms is 6 + 12 + 6 = 24.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0941.explanation: In a neutral atom, the number of protons equals the number of electrons, so the overall charge is zero. For example, helium with atomic number 2 has 2 protons and 2 electrons when stable.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0942.explanation: Ionic bonding occurs when electrons are transferred from one atom to another. This transfer results in the formation of positive ions (cations) and negative ions (anions), which are held together by electrostatic attractions.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0943.explanation: In solids, particles are closely packed and held together by strong intermolecular forces. They vibrate and rotate about fixed positions but do not have translational motion, which gives solids their definite shape and volume.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0944.explanation: The law of definite proportions states that a given compound always contains its constituent elements in a fixed (definite) ratio by mass, which corresponds to simple whole number ratios of atoms.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0945.explanation: In the reaction between dichromate and bisulfite, Cr₂O₇²⁻ (Cr in +6) is reduced to Cr³⁺, and HSO₃⁻ (S in +4) is oxidized to HSO₄⁻ (S in +6). Thus, HSO₃⁻ is the reducing agent and is oxidized.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0946.explanation: Moving from left to right across a period, the atomic number increases by one, meaning one more proton and one more electron are added.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0947.explanation: Initial rate = k[A][B]. New rate = k[2A][3B] = k × 2 × 3 × [A][B] = 6 × k[A][B]. Factor = 6.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0948.explanation: The reaction requires 2 moles of I⁻ for every 1 mole of Pb²⁺. Moles of Pb²⁺ = 0.700 mol. Moles of I⁻ needed = 2 × 0.700 = 1.40 mol. HI provides I⁻ in a 1:1 ratio, so moles of HI needed = 1.40 mol. Volume of HI solution = moles / concentration = 1.40 mol / 3.550 M = 0.394 L = 394 mL.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0949.explanation: In physics and chemistry, energy is defined as the capacity to perform work.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0950.explanation: Metabolism encompasses all biochemical processes that break down food molecules to release energy for the body.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0951.explanation: Molar mass N₂ = 28 g/mol, so 28 g N₂ = 1 mol N₂. From equation, 1 mol N₂ requires 3 mol H₂. Mass of 3 mol H₂ = 3 mol × 2 g/mol = 6 g.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0952.explanation: Aristotle rejected Democritus's atomic theory and believed that matter was continuous and could be divided infinitely, not composed of indivisible particles.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0953.explanation: Initial rate = k[A][B]². New rate = k[2A][2B]² = k × 2 × 4 × [A][B]² = 8 × k[A][B]². Factor = 8.

uni-unilag-chm101-bank-0954.explanation: Assume 100 g: moles P = 43.64/30.974 = 1.409, moles O = 56.36/15.999 = 3.523. Ratio P:O = 1.409/1.409 : 3.523/1.409 = 1:2.5 = 2:5.
